title: Find original sources for the AddBiomechanics studies and test GRF-only extraction

decision_context.answer_note_premise: AddBiomechanics adds predicted GRF; add only that column if obtainable without the full download.

summary: José's premise does not hold: AddBiomechanics 1.0 GRF are measured force-plate data, assigned to the feet and possibly filtered per processing pass; frames without trusted GRF are kept and flagged, not predicted. The legacy files came from older converters that wrote one row per frame from processingPasses[1] (70 kg mass fallback in cc94be4), so extra legacy rows are most plausibly the kept flagged frames, not pass expansion (download page, ECCV dataset paper, PLoS ONE 2023 paper, B3D schema). Predicted GRF exist only as benchmark baselines. GRF-only extraction: the archive host supports single and multi-range requests and any zip member can be fetched alone, but members are deflate-compressed, so GRF needs the whole member. The official Google Drive tree also serves each subject's uncompressed B3D with single-range (not multi-range) support. B3D layout confirmed on one 0.5 MB member: int64 header length, header protobuf, then fixed-size records (sensor frame plus one frame per pass); GRF fields are about 3% of each record, interleaved in every frame. So a GRF-only partial read needs about one HTTP request per frame (about 10^7 for these studies, estimated) and is not practical. The practical route streams each No_Arm member and keeps only the GRF: 153.1 GB transferred for all 11, 22.3 GB for fa16+ta21+ta22, peak disk 1.64 GB. Originals: eight studies have full originals with markers and force plates (ca23, mo15, ti19, vz22, wa23 known; new: ha13 and fr12 on SimTK with an MIT-style license and login required, ha23 GroundLink with no data license stated). ta22 has only the authors' right-stance windows (SimTK HDF5, 1.98 GB); the README points to AddBiomechanics for the full marker/force data. fa16 has no original found. ta21's supposed author Drive folder is the official AddBiomechanics Drive folder Tan2021_Formatted_No_Arm. For the eight studies, AddBiomechanics GRF would duplicate measured GRF already in the originals.

remaining: D-HIST-03-1 (José): source for the three studies without a full original (Falisse, Tan running, Tan walking).

José's D-HIST-01-1 note assumed AddBiomechanics GRF are predicted; the coordinator should tell him they are measured plate data (duplicates for the eight studies with originals), so no separate GRF column is planned for those eight. Legacy extra rows: the legacy converters wrote one row per frame (processingPasses[1]); the plausible cause is kept GRF-flagged frames, unverified against legacy files.

Not checked: inner formats of SimTK and Wang archives; GroundLink data license; kneeloads competitions 1-3 license; whether the six kneeloads subjects are distinct people; participant crosswalks (Moore 15 vs 12, Wang 12 vs 9, Tan running 16 vs 8); whether No_Arm and With_Arm GRF are identical; frame sizes for any B3D but one; Falisse manuscript text; Drive quotas.

For HIST-01/02: legacy converters read processingPasses[1], which in Subject29 is the low-pass-filter pass (order kinematics, lowPassFilter, dynamics), not dynamics; legacy angles/moments/GRF may come from a pre-dynamics pass. One subject checked.
HIST-01 record ta21 original_data ('Author Google Drive folder') should be corrected to 'AddBiomechanics official Drive copy' when HIST-01 artifacts are next rebuilt.
Licensing for redistribution of ha23 (no stated data license) and fr12 competitions 1-3 must be settled before any release that includes them.

decisions.question: Three historical studies have no complete original data outside AddBiomechanics: Falisse (none found), Tan running (only the AddBiomechanics copy), and Tan walking (the authors share only cut-out right-foot stance steps). AddBiomechanics force data turned out to be measured plate forces, not predictions. What should LocoHub do with these three?

options.label: Keep all three archived
options.consequence: Pages stay labelled legacy with corrected citations; nothing downloaded; no new adapter. Reversible.

options.label: Tan walking from the authors' stance steps; archive the other two
options.consequence: About 2 GB; one new adapter; only right-leg stance windows, not full strides or continuous recordings. Reversible.

options.label: AddBiomechanics for all three
options.consequence: About 22 GB transferred one participant at a time, under 2 GB on disk at once; measured forces. The current adapter writes 4 rows per frame (raw plus 3 passes) and keeps flagged frames: about 15 million rows (rough estimate); output size not estimated. No converter change assumed. Reversible.

decisions.options_order: By data to download: none, about 2 GB, about 22 GB.
decisions.cost_of_waiting: The three pages stay legacy and unreviewed; the other eight studies can proceed from their originals; no active dataset is affected.
decisions.why: C is the only complete source for all three, and streaming keeps disk use under 2 GB. The premise behind avoiding AddBiomechanics (predicted forces) does not hold, but the rows-and-storage cost remains and the output size is unestimated, and José's note preferred originals over AddBiomechanics, so this needs his fresh choice. A is the low-cost alternative if derivatives are unwanted.
decisions.check: Open the Tan running Google Drive folder from the HIST-01 record: its title is 'Tan2021_Formatted_No_Arm', an AddBiomechanics export name.
